question: Should experiment-gated Claw lifecycle ownership diagnostics become a core doctor check as part of the open Claws RFC stack?
rationale: The open RFC treats the implementation as prototype evidence and reserves acceptance and compatibility for a separate decision, so patch correctness cannot determine permanent product ownership.

options.title: Sponsor the core doctor surface
options.body: Confirm that core doctor owns these experiment-gated findings after the read-only state defect is fixed.

options.title: Keep diagnostics in Claws status
options.body: Limit lifecycle diagnostics to the feature-specific CLI until the RFC establishes a broader doctor contract.

options.title: Pause the stack slice
options.body: Keep this draft unlanded until the RFC and preceding ownership slices are accepted.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the core doctor surface
recommendation.body: Confirm that core doctor owns these experiment-gated findings after the read-only state defect is fixed.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared state database and core doctor framework history make @steipete the best available owner for the core ownership decision, with the RFC author supplying feature context.
